description: Summonable thinking prompts during a freewrite. Mid-sprint the writer can summon a single one-line dimensional question — a 'spark' — that names a lens their draft hasn't used. The AI never renders, signals, or animates unbidden: a spark card appears only when summoned, fades on the first keystroke, offers exactly one alternative, and never returns on its own. The writing surface stays interruption-free.
preamble: Requires the dev server started with E2E_TESTING=true E2E_BYPASS_AUTH=true bun run dev. E2E_TESTING selects the deterministic mock spark model (so the served questions are fixed stand-ins, not real model output) and an in-memory event store; E2E_BYPASS_AUTH lets /editor load without OAuth. Spark is active only while a sprint is in the running phase. Summon a spark either by pressing the summon hotkey — Cmd+period on Mac, Ctrl+period otherwise, with the editor focused — or by clicking the small, static spark affordance at the bottom-right edge of the writing surface. A spark needs a minimum amount of draft to ground on (about fifteen words); below that, a summon is a deliberate quiet no-op. The contract to protect throughout: nothing about spark renders, pulses, badges, or animates until the writer summons it.

workflows.name: Summoning mid-sprint renders exactly one one-line question
steps: Clear local storage and navigate to /editor.
From the wizard, start a sprint.
Type a few sentences of a draft (at least twenty words) about some topic, then stop typing.
Summon a spark (press the summon hotkey or click the small spark affordance at the bottom-right edge of the surface).
Verify a single spark card appears at the edge of the surface, near the affordance — never at the cursor and never overlaying the draft text.
Verify the card contains exactly one short question on a single line, ending in a single question mark, with no preamble and no second question.
Verify the freewrite text itself is untouched — the card adds a question beside the surface, it does not edit or annotate the draft.

workflows.name: Typing fades the card, and it does not return unbidden
steps: Start a sprint and type at least twenty words, then stop.
Summon a spark and confirm one card is showing.
Resume typing a few words into the draft.
Verify the spark card fades out and disappears after the first keystrokes.
Continue writing for several more seconds and pause again without summoning.
Verify no spark card reappears on its own — once it has faded it stays gone until the writer summons again.

workflows.name: 'Different spark' yields exactly one alternative, then the option disappears
steps: Start a sprint, type at least twenty words, then stop.
Summon a spark and confirm one card with a question is showing.
Note the wording of the first question, then click the 'Different spark' control on the card.
Verify the card now shows one alternative question that differs from the first.
Verify the 'Different spark' control is gone after that single use — there is no way to re-roll a second time.
Verify only one card is present the whole time; re-rolling replaces the question in place, it does not stack a second card.

workflows.name: A full sprint with no summon shows zero spark UI beyond the static affordance
steps: Clear local storage and navigate to /editor, then start a sprint.
Note the appearance of the small spark affordance at the bottom-right edge of the surface.
Type a full sentence, then stop typing for about four seconds to force a real pause.
Type another sentence, then pause for about four seconds again.
Type a third sentence, then pause for about four seconds a final time — this drives the background preparation that the contract says must stay invisible.
Throughout the writing and all three pauses, verify no spark card, question, or prompt ever appears anywhere on the surface.
Verify the spark affordance never pulses, badges, spins, animates, or changes appearance — it looks identical at every moment, whether the writer is typing or paused.
Verify the writing surface stays completely quiet — no shimmer, no 'thinking' indicator, nothing that signals the writer is being watched.

workflows.name: Summoning very early still serves a broad spark (graceful degradation)
steps: Start a sprint and type just two short sentences — roughly fifteen to twenty words — then stop.
Summon a spark.
Verify a single spark card still appears with one one-line question, rather than nothing — with only a little draft to work from, a broad dimension is served instead of a sharp one.
Note: because the model layer is mocked, the exact wording is a fixed stand-in; the point is that an early summon degrades gracefully to a broad question instead of failing.

workflows.name: Summoning with almost nothing written quietly does nothing
steps: Start a fresh sprint and type only a handful of words — well under a dozen — then stop.
Summon a spark.
Verify nothing renders at all: no spark card, no placeholder, no question, and no error or message.
Verify the spark affordance is unchanged and gives no feedback — the summon is a deliberate quiet no-op because there is not yet enough draft to ground a question on.
Type several more words so the draft comfortably clears twenty words, stop, and summon again.
Verify a spark card now appears — once there is enough ground, the same summon works.

workflows.name: Pausing and resuming the sprint keeps sparks working in the same sprint
steps: Start a sprint and type at least twenty words, then stop.
Pause the sprint using the timer's pause control.
Try to summon a spark while paused and verify nothing renders — spark is active only while the sprint is running.
Resume the sprint using the play control.
Summon a spark now that the sprint is running again.
Verify a single spark card appears — pausing and resuming does not end the sprint or reset spark, so sparks still work in the same sprint.

workflows.name: Escape dismisses a card, and a dismissed spark does not reappear
steps: Start a sprint, type at least twenty words, then stop.
Summon a spark and confirm one card is showing.
Press Escape.
Verify the spark card fades out and disappears.
Pause for several seconds and then continue writing without summoning.
Verify the dismissed spark does not reappear on its own at any point — dismissal is final until the writer summons again.
